newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Livshits sees budget back pay cleared by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Livshits sees budget back pay cleared by year-end.

text.p: Russian Finance Minister Alexander Livshits said on Wednesday all salary arrears due to be paid by the federal government would be cleared by the end of the year, Itar-Tass news agency said.
Livshits, attending the first meeting of a conciliation commission designed to iron out the 1997 draft budget, said clearing the debts was one of the government's key tasks.
He said a new draft of the budget, which the State Duma lower house of parlaiment rejected on a first reading, was in line with deputies' recommendations.
Livshits said the social aspect of the budget had been strengthened and investment parameters had been re-examined.

He said a new addition to the budget draft was an article on financing military reform. It was planned to raise spending on conversion of military production and to increase demand for military exports to Commonwealth of Independent States members.
Changes in the financing of scientific research were also planned
"All this makee the 1997 draft budget acceptable for adoption by the State Duma," Livshits said.
Livshits said the government was prepared to countenance modifications to the overall budget parameters, including the deficit, but only to a very limited extent, Interfax news agency said.
The new draft budget cut planned revenues to 432.8 trillion roubles from 433.64 trillion in the first draft and trimmed expenditures to 523.5 trillion roubles from 524.34 trillion.
The budget deficit remains unchanged at 3.3 percent of gross domestic product, or 90.70 trillion roubles.
